steps.note: linear-network-roles.md says only generically that the network 'exchanges two banks of values with prescribed signs and restores every auxiliary value'. subset-intersection-construction.md gives h=100, triples, N=binom(h,3)^3 and D=h^3 (the paper's m), and works out the F2 gather/scatter/side-wire coefficient that leaves only g_S. But no page names the data pairs X_a,Y_a indexed by a in T^3, gives the map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), or shows how three stages of invocations compose into the exchange (paper 653-765). The pieces are scattered across pages and the exchange itself is never stated, so the conservative verdict is mentioned. A reason is given: 'Each fixed-tape procedure of the argument comes from one such network.'

The page defines frames D_nu as invertible operators acting within one wire's array, and an edge as changing the stored array by D_beta D_alpha^{-1}. It shows G(D f_1,...,D f_p)=D G(f_1,...,f_p), and the telescoping gives eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} on each route, matching paper 793-825 route by route. The global form D_out S D_in^{-1} is not written. The page never says why frames are introduced: that the endpoint frames can be made the shear while the intermediate frames are chosen so each edge is cheap (paper 823-825). It says only that the page 'explains how a network computes its result on an array'.

The 'Labels' paragraph gives the form I-J/9, <t_T,t_S>=|T cap S|-1, and the space F=(Q^h)^{tensor 3} of dimension D=h^3. It defines a label as a nondegenerate subspace and gives U_iota as a line and one side-wire growth (h-2). 'Counting' says each central wire loses h on 'a decreasing edge'. Three things are missing: the actual gate label assignment (the paper's table 975-988); the assertion that every edge joins comparable labels (it appears only as the hypothesis 'If U subset V'); and the statement that the central 3->4 edges are the only decreasing edges (lemma, 997-1010). Those are what let rank=dimension change apply on every edge, so the verdict is the conservative mentioned. The reason is implicit but present: the page passes straight from labels to projections, ranks and smaller calls.

Stated explicitly: 'If U subseteq V, then P_V-P_U is the identity on V cap U^perp and zero on U oplus V^perp, so its rank is dim V - dim U.' The source exception is also there: 'The first edge out of each source has matrix 2P_{U_iota}, rank one, with no label change.' This matches paper 1156-1166. The reason given is 'Each unit of rank costs one smaller call.'

The page says signed changes telescope and gate labels cancel, source dimensions sum to N, and sinks have dimension D except the N with label U_iota^perp, so the signed total is WD-2N. It gives L=3 binom(h,3)^2 h^2 (=Ich with c=h), adds 2L for absolute values, and adds N source ranks to get s=WD-N+2L. This matches paper 1003-1006 and 1148-1151. One slip: it says 'Sources have dimension 1' although only the X_a sources do, but the sum N is right. address-shear-factorization.md and main-theorem.md restate s_b=W_bR-N+2L_b.

subset-intersection-construction.md: 'L/N=3h^2/binom(h,3)=100/539, so 2L<N and s<WD.' This is correct: 30000/161700=100/539. The complex 101/539 is not given, but fast-butterfly-layers.md gives the complex deficit 73/19906842167500. The reason is given: s<Wm is 'the paper's decisive property', and recursive-power-saving.md says 'The saving exists because s/W<m.'

The conclusion is asserted: 'The address shear is the endpoint operator of the bit network', and 'the network's endpoint operator is the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D)'. linear-network-roles.md says every role, scratch included, keeps the endpoint operator. Two things are missing. No page states the identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, or why it holds (P_{U^perp}+P_U=I on X_a; 0->I on the other roles, paper 1169-1171). No page states that the frame at a vertex with matrix M is the address shear Phi_M (paper 1124-1132, 1514-1528). So the source matrix -P_U on the subset page is never connected to the shear; main-theorem.md only names the 'negative source projection'. The reason is given: fast-address-interchange.md says the network performs the middle update of the three-update swap.

The page gives M=F_1 Pi F_2 with invertible lower-triangular F_i and Pi having rank(M) ones, with an elimination proof. It gives the conjugation procedure and the one-interchange implementation of H_sigma<-H_sigma+D_tau. It concludes 'the shear needs rank_Q M interchanges plus O(V) further work', with lower-triangular passes costing O(V). It adds 'Each edge of the bit network carries such a matrix. The interchange count of the network is s_b, the sum of their ranks.' This matches paper 1364-1447. One misleading phrase in the opening box: the factorization 'reduces rank', when it actually makes the cost equal to the rank.

fast-address-interchange.md says each of the s calls acts on a role stream of volume V/W. It gives Q_0=O(1), Q_k<=(s/W)Q_{k-1}+C, 'fix tau<1 with s/W<m^tau', and the geometric-sum argument for both cases, giving O(Vu^tau). This matches paper 1543-1557. The explicit value tau=1-2^{-50} and the deficit check (paper 1319-1346) appear only for the companion complex network's sigma (fast-butterfly-layers.md), not for the bit network's tau. The page also measures chunks in bits rather than radix-q digits; main-theorem.md corrects this. recursive-power-saving.md gives the general version.

links.note: linear-network-roles.md introduces the network and then its frames.
linear-network-roles.md links to subset-intersection-construction.md in its 'Used by' list and connections map, though not in the body text.
On subset-intersection-construction.md, the rank fact is followed by the N/L budget.
On subset-intersection-construction.md, s=WD-N+2L is followed by L/N=100/539.

subset-intersection-construction.md links only to linear-network-roles.md (general endpoint telescoping), the glossary and recursive-power-saving.md. The shear statement sits on address-shear-factorization.md and fast-address-interchange.md, reachable only through linear-network-roles.md or recursive-power-saving.md.
address-shear-factorization.md states that the endpoint operator is the shear and then factors the shear.
address-shear-factorization.md links to fast-address-interchange.md (Used by / connections), which has the recurrence.

breaks.note: The network's scalar action (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) through three stages of invocations is never stated. The banks indexed by triples are never named. The F2 coefficient calculation on the subset page is not tied to the bank exchange.
Frames and their telescoping are explained, but not why: to make the endpoint operator a chosen shear while the edge frame changes carry the cost.

There is no gate label assignment. That every edge joins comparable labels, and that the central 3->4 edges are the only decreasing ones, is never asserted. So the reader cannot see that rank=dimension change covers every edge.

The endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and frames-as-address-shears Phi_M are absent. The reader is told the endpoint operator is the shear but never sees why the -P_U source and P_{U^perp} sink give it.
From the s<Wm count on subset-intersection-construction.md there is no direct link to the pages that turn the network into a shear (address-shear-factorization.md, fast-address-interchange.md).

summary: W1 carries the reader well through the counting core (rank = dimension change, the budget WD-N+2L, L/N=100/539) on one page. It also covers the factorization into rank-many interchanges and the recurrence to O(Vu^tau), so the network-to-exponent arc is recognizable. The chain thins at both ends of the counting core. The network's actual bank exchange and the gate label assignment (comparability, the only decreasing edges) are not reconstructed. The endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m, which turns labels and projections into the shear H<-H+D, is only asserted, and no direct link joins the count to the shear page.
